newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda abruptly resigned yesterday, creating a growing vacuum within Thai financial circles and leaving behind some urgent unsettled issues, such as balancing the 1997 budget and granting three new domestic banking licences. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- A Chart Thai faction led by deputy party leader Vatana Asavahame has decided to defect to the Prachakorn Thai Party, following a serious conflict with Chart Thai leader Banharn Silpa-archa. Vatana says he has been asked to field suitable election candidates but had never received cooperation from the Chart Thai party leader in the past. (MATICHON)

- The Public Health Ministry should review its 4.6 billion baht purchasing programme to supply a large number of medical apparatus and laboratory equipment to community health centres throughout the country because of irregularities in the way it was drawn up. A committee member says that the budget requested for the acquisition plan appears to be excessively higher than the market price. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand will wait until next month to gather all economic data from January to November before making its 1997 economic forecast. The central bank was scheduled to complete its economic forecast by the end of this month, based on the data from the first nine months. (THE NATION)

- The Commerce Ministry has announced a plan to clean out existing export stocks quickly in a bid to boost exports by one billion baht by the end of the year. The proposal, which will initially focus on getting rid of garment stocks, was laid out at yesterday's meeting chaired by Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa. (BANGKOK POST)
